entry.standardEnglish: ASV throughout, incl. 'so that there is no house, no entering in', 'Be still', 'the Shihor', 'the mart of nations', 'virgins', 'When the report cometh to Egypt', 'joyous [city]', 'rejoice', 'the bestower of crowns', 'traffickers', 'the honorable of the earth', 'to stain … to bring into contempt', 'there is no restraint any more', 'the Assyrian founded it for them that dwell in the wilderness; they set up their towers … they made it a ruin', 'according to the days of one king', 'harp', 'make sweet melody', 'visit', 'holiness to Jehovah', 'durable clothing'; JPS 1917 'Shihor', 'the crowning city', 'pollute', 'no girdle', 'for shipmen', 'remember', 'stately clothing'; NJPS 'Moan', 'crown-wearing Tyre', 'defile', 'This is a harbor no more', 'Assyria, which founded it for ships', 'equaling the lifetime of one king', 'lyre', 'take note of', 'consecrated to the LORD', 'clothe themselves elegantly'; KJV 23:5 'As at the report concerning Egypt' (ASV via bible-api.com; JPS 1917 and NJPS 1985 via Sefaria API v3; checked 2026-11-26). LXX Isa 23:10 ἐργάζου τὴν γῆν σου … πλοῖα οὐκέτι ἔρχεται ἐκ Καρχηδόνος (Rahlfs 1935, checked by the Reviewer 2026-11-26). NRSV readings recalled, not verified.
entry.wohChoice: 23:1 privative 'so that there is no house, no entering in' (ASV, JPS 1917); NJPS construal and the harbor sense in commentary. Place names: 'Tarshish', 'ships of Tarshish' (as 2:16; wave I-4 ruling 8), 'Kittim' (23:1, 12, qere), 'Shihor' without the article (MT, JPS 1917, NJPS; against ASV 'the Shihor'), 'Canaan' (23:11), 'Chaldeans' (23:13, as 13:19; 43:14; 48:14, 20; central eretz-kasdim not applied); identifications (Cyprus, a Nile branch, Phoenicia, Babylonia) in commentary only. 23:2 MT 'Be still … you whom the merchants of Sidon, crossing the sea, have filled' (ASV); NJPS 'Moan' and the 1QIsaᵃ mlʾkyk 'your messengers' in commentary. 23:3 'the market of nations'. 23:4 and 23:12 bᵉṯûlāh 'virgin(s)' (ASV, JPS 1917). 23:5 temporal 'When the report comes to Egypt' (ASV). 23:7 'jubilant city' ('city' supplied) and 23:12 'exult' for the root ʿlz, kept apart from śmḥ 'rejoice'. 23:8 'the bestower of crowns' (ASV); kinʿāneyhā 'traders'; niḵbaddê-ʾāreṣ 'the honored of the earth' (23:8, 9; as 43:4 'you are honored'). 23:9 lᵉḥallēl 'to profane', lᵉhāqēl 'to bring into contempt' (the qll/kbd wordplay in commentary). 23:10 MT and ASV 'there is no restraint any more'; NJPS 'harbor', the LXX 'work your land … ships no longer come from Carthage' (Rahlfs) and the 'ships of Tarshish' emendation (partial LXX support) in commentary. 23:11 māʿuzneyhā 'its strongholds'. 23:13 MT and ASV in the line, 'Behold, the land of the Chaldeans! This people was not; Assyria founded it for those who dwell in the wilderness. They set up his siege towers, they overthrew its palaces; he made it a ruin' (qere, MT number kept); repunctuation, kittîm emendation, 'ships' and gloss theories in commentary. 23:15 'like the days of one king'. 23:16 kinnôr 'lyre' (as 5:12; 24:8), 'play skillfully'. 23:17 pqd 'visit' (ASV) for the restoration sense. 23:18 'holiness to YHWH' (ASV, JPS 1917), 'durable clothing' (ASV) with 'stately / fine' in commentary.
entry.rationale: Each item is a site where the Translator asked the Editor to choose between standard renderings. The Editor keeps the Masoretic Text and the public-domain baseline (ASV, checked with JPS 1917 and NJPS 1985 on Sefaria) unless the book's concordance requires a change. Every alternative is recorded in commentary, no item adopts an emendation, and no item carries a project reading. The place names follow wave I-4 ruling 4, with ASV spellings for names that no entry fixes. The one exception is Shihor: MT has no article, and JPS 1917 and NJPS omit it. The ʿlz and kbd choices keep the root concordance of the book (32:13 'the jubilant city'; 43:4 'you are honored'). The Niphal participle niḵbaddê is a verbal form, not the noun kāḇôḏ, so the strict 'glory' rule of wave I-4 ruling 2 does not apply to it. At 23:13 all three PD references and NRSV construe the verse differently, and NJPS marks it 'Meaning of verse uncertain'. The line therefore follows MT with ASV's wording and keeps MT's shift of number, which ASV smooths, while the commentary gives the repunctuation, the kittîm emendation (NJPS note), the 'ships' reading of ṣiyyîm (JPS 1917, NJPS) and the gloss hypothesis. Two of the Translator's attributions were corrected after checking. 'Remember' at 23:17 is JPS 1917; NJPS reads 'take note of'. At 23:10 the reported 1QIsaᵃ reading 'ships of Tarshish' is not supported by the online collation of col. XVIII by Fred P. Miller (ao.net/~fmoeller), which lists no variant there. The scroll readings cited (23:2 mlʾkyk; 23:11, 13, 15) come from that collation and were not checked against DJD 32. pqd 'visit' at 23:17 is deliberately kept apart from the judgment rendering 'punished' of yippaqedu-pqd-visitation-imprisonment-isaiah-24, because here the visitation restores Tyre. All choices are standard renderings, so the claim is direct.

rationaleAppend: Wave I-4 (23:1): maśśāʾ ṣōr 'The oracle concerning Tyre', as at 13:1 and 15:1. ASV and JPS 1917 'The burden of Tyre'; NJPS 'The "Tyre" Pronouncement' (ASV via bible-api.com; JPS 1917 and NJPS 1985 via Sefaria API v3; checked 2026-11-26).

Wave I-4 (Isa 23): the Translator's descriptive title 'Isaiah 23 — The oracle concerning Tyre: the ships of Tarshish wail, and Tyre's seventy years' is ratified; it carries no lens. Quotation marks: the sea's speech (23:4) and YHWH's word to Sidon (23:12, to the end of the verse, as NJPS; JPS 1917 closes after 'rejoice'); the song of the prostitute (23:16), introduced by a colon at the end of 23:15, quoted under the house rule for embedded speech although ASV and JPS 1917 print it without marks and NJPS sets it as verse (ASV via bible-api.com; JPS 1917 and NJPS 1985 via Sefaria API v3; checked 2026-11-26).

Wave I-4 (Isa 23): the qere is translated at 23:12 (ketiv כתיים, qere כִּתִּים 'Kittim', spelling only) and 23:13 (ketiv בחיניו, qere בַחוּנָיו 'his siege towers'). Orchestrator: add '23:12' and '23:13' to the qere list in wohChoice on merge (scope-only change; the field is not rewritten here to avoid conflicts). MT is kept and variants are reported in commentary at 23:2 (1QIsaᵃ mlʾkyk 'your messengers' for millᵉʾûḵ; NRSV follows, recalled), 23:10 (the 'ships of Tarshish' emendation reported in an NJPS note, with partial support in the LXX's 'ships'; NJPS mēzaḥ 'harbor'; LXX (Rahlfs) ἐργάζου τὴν γῆν σου 'work your land', i.e. ʿbdy for ʿbry; the Translator's claim that 1QIsaᵃ reads 'ships of Tarshish' is not supported by the online collation), 23:13 (repunctuation; kittîm for kaśdîm; 1QIsaᵃ feminine suffixes) and 23:15 (1QIsaᵃ omission by homoioteleuton). The 1QIsaᵃ readings come from Fred P. Miller's online collation (ao.net/~fmoeller) of col. XVIII and were not checked against DJD 32.

Wave I-4 extension, limited to the ʾî item: yōšᵉḇê ʾî at 23:2 and 23:6 is 'inhabitants of the coastland', concordant with 11:11, 24:15, 40:15 and 20:6 (ASV 'the coast', JPS 1917 'coast-land', NJPS 'coastland dwellers', checked on Sefaria and bible-api.com). Here it is the Phoenician coast together with island Tyre.

Wave I-4 (Isa 23): 'Egypt' (23:5) and 'Assyria' (23:13, ASV 'the Assyrian') take the English forms fixed by the wave rulings, as at Isa 20. Tyre and Sidon also take the English forms (ruling 4), against JPS 1917 'Zidon'.

Wave I-4 (Isa 23): 'the earth' in niḵbaddê-ʾāreṣ 'the honored of the earth' (23:8, 9; ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS 'the world') and kol-mamlᵉḵôṯ hāʾāreṣ 'all the kingdoms of the earth' (23:17; ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS 'of the world'), the universal horizon of Tyre's trade. Territorial ʾereṣ in 23:1, 10, 13 stays 'land' under the central eretz entry.

Wave I-4 extension (Isa 23): gᵉʾôn kol-ṣᵉḇî at 23:9, the pride that YHWH profanes, is 'pride' (ASV and JPS 1917 'the pride of all glory'; NJPS folds the phrase into 'all glorious beauty', checked on Sefaria). The recorded departure from the default 'majesty' (hadar-splendor-isaiah) applies, as at 13:19 and 16:6.
